content:
- Model consistently underestimates true price movements, especially after sentiment turns negative (e.g., -0.16, -0.11, -0.16) — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for each negative sentiment shift.
- Forecast shows strong upward bias early in the 30-day horizon, then flattens — correct by adding a downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day after day 10 if sentiment remains neutral or negative.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 89.06 → 93.62), model overreacts and overshoots — cap forecast at 10% above recent peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- When sentiment is neutral or positive (all 0.00), model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.0% daily offset to forecast to catch up with true price.
- Mean reversion is weak in early days — if forecast is below 85.0 and sentiment is neutral, increase by 0.3% per day until sentiment shifts or price crosses 87.0.
